title: Post-train quant sensitivity sweep for KV-cache saturation and batching interactions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Characterize end-to-end latency and throughput regressions introduced by post-training quantized variants (FP8/INT8) under KV-cache saturation and mixed-batch long-context workloads. Validate calibration workflows to maintain <1.5% macro-F1 degradation on downstream QA/eval tasks and identify batching thresholds where tail latency exceeds SLO.

Success criteria: 
- Throughput/latency matrix across batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16,32] and context lengths [512,2048,8192] for FP8 and INT8 variants.
- Calibration acceptance criteria (per-layer scale update) that keeps accuracy drop <=1.5% vs FP16 baseline on the in-house QA eval set.
- Identify safe batching window for production (max batch size per sequence length) where 99th percentile latency < 200ms on p4d-equivalent nodes.

Plan: 
1) Generate calibrated FP8 and INT8 variants using the updated calibration pipeline (post-train symmetric/asymmetric per-kernel options). Store calibration artifacts with hash tags.
2) Run microbench harness to measure kernel-level ops (matmul GEMM, softmax) to detect saturation under KV-cache heavy sequences.
3) Run end-to-end load generator with mixed batching and long-context traces derived from production sampling (anonymized). Capture token-level latencies, batching efficiency, KV hit/miss statistics.
4) Run accuracy validations: zero-shot QA and prompt completion evals; compute macro-F1 and perplexity deltas.

Instrumentation: Perf dashboards (Grafana): token-latency, per-batch throughput, GPU SM utilization, memory allocs, KV cache hit-rate, GEMM queue times. Store raw traces in S3 for post-mortem.

Deliverables:
- Throughput/latency CSV matrix and heatmaps for FP8/INT8
- Calibration configs that pass accuracy threshold or detailed rejection rationale
- Runbook recommendations: default batch caps per seq length, KV-cache warmup settings, and fallback policy thresholds

Risks/assumptions:
- Calibration dataset may not cover rare tokens affecting tail regen quality.
- Hardware baseline approximates p4d; results may shift on different card types.

Contact and owners: lead engineer Lucas Gomez, calibration SME Mei Chen, evaluator Sasha Ivanov.
comments: 2025-10-14: Kickoff notes — calibration pipeline branch created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib/compare/PR-214). Assigned Lucas to run initial microbench.

2025-10-20: Microbench results posted to dashboard: small GEMM kernels show 12-18% latency inflation for INT8 with per-channel asymmetric scales under KV saturation. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant/microbench-suite
2025-10-27: Calibration pass produced FP8 variant with macro-F1 delta 0.9% and INT8 delta 1.7% on our QA set. Decided to iterate calibration hyperparams for INT8 (per-layer clip vs per-channel).

2025-11-01: End-to-end load run (mixed batches) uploaded: s3://redwood-experiments/ENG-78190/run-20251101/; observed 99p latency 220ms for batch=8, seq=2048 on INT8 — exceeds SLO. Action: experiment with lower batch caps and KV-cache coalescing.

2025-11-03: Design review with PM and runtime — agreed on staged rollout: enable FP8 default on dedicated pools, INT8 gated behind additional calibration and a canary policy. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/608
